newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Kohl says unsure about achieving jobs target.
newsitem.headline: Kohl says unsure about achieving jobs target.

text.p: Chancellor Helmut Kohl said on Thursday he was not sure if the government could achieve its goal of halving unemployment by the year 2000, but said he expected progress this year.

Unemployment is hovering at a record 4.7 million, the highest level since the 1930s, and is a threat to the country's efforts to meet tough fiscal targets for joining European economic and monetary union in 1999.

In an interview with ARD television from his Easter holiday resort in Austria, Kohl said he expected a "slightly flattening out" of unemployment levels this year, but that he was "not entirely certain" the government could meet its jobs target.
Kohl has in the past expressed doubts about being able to meet this jobs target, but he has refused to abandon the goal entirely, although few economists conisider it realistic.
The chancellor attacked the opposition Social Democrats for blocking economic reforms that he said were key to set the stage for investment that would create new jobs.
"Investors will come as soon as the SPD gives up its blockade," he said.
